findings.location: package.json engines ("node": ">=18"), README.md 'Install' + SKILL.md frontmatter `compatibility: ... Node.js 18+` vs package-lock.json (playwright 1.62.1, whose package.json declares engines node >=20)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: the lockfile pins playwright 1.62.1 and node_modules/playwright/package.json and playwright-core/package.json both declare `engines.node >= 20`, while the repo advertises Node 18+. A first-time user on Node 18 following the README gets EBADENGINE warnings from `npm run setup` and an unsupported Playwright runtime; the first public issue filed will be 'does not work on the Node version you say you support'.
findings.amendment: Set package.json `engines.node` to `>=20` and change 'Node.js 18+' to 'Node.js 20+' in README.md and SKILL.md `compatibility`; CI already uses node 20 so no workflow change is needed.
findings.mechanical_test: grep -q '"node": ">=20"' package.json && ! grep -rn 'Node.js 18' README.md SKILL.md && node -e "const l=require('./package-lock.json');const v=l.packages['node_modules/playwright'].version;console.log(v)" prints a version whose node_modules/playwright/package.json engines.node is satisfied by package.json engines.node.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs lines 450-458 (screenshots[].path = join(config.outDir,...) absolute), line 310 (spec.path = resolve(value)), line 322 (config.chrome), lines 222-235 attest, lines 253-260 check; docs/example/run-1/receipt.json and run-2/receipt.json (paths `/tmp/demo/...`)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: every receipt stores absolute filesystem paths for PNGs, snapshots, the --spec file, and --chrome. On a user's machine that is `/home/<username>/project/...` — the receipt users are told to share (README 'The report an agent hands back should quote the run_id, the check result, and the attestation notes') leaks the OS username and directory layout. Second consequence, OBSERVED: `check` verifies bytes at the recorded absolute path, not next to the receipt: I copied a run directory elsewhere and `check` on the copy still exited 0 because it hashed the ORIGINAL files; the committed docs/example receipts cannot be `check`ed at all (paths point at /tmp/demo, which the README has to apologise for). A receipt shipped to another machine or reviewer is therefore un-checkable, and tampering the shipped copy is undetectable while the original exists.
findings.amendment: Record `path` relative to the receipt's directory (e.g. `desktop--overview--viewport.png`) in capture; in attest/check resolve `join(dirname(receiptPath), shot.path)` when the stored path is relative (keep accepting absolute paths for old receipts). Store `spec.path` as given by the user rather than resolved, and store `chrome` only when explicitly passed. Regenerate docs/example receipts so they contain relative paths, and delete the README sentence excusing `/tmp/demo`.
findings.mechanical_test: After a capture into `./.agent-verification/x`, `grep -c '"path": "/' .agent-verification/x/receipt.json` prints 0; `cp -r .agent-verification/x /some/other/dir && node scripts/capture.mjs check /some/other/dir/x/receipt.json` reports UNINSPECTED/OK for the copied files (and a byte-appended PNG in the copy yields STALE ATTESTATION, exit 3); `node scripts/capture.mjs check docs/example/run-2/receipt.json` exits 0 in a fresh clone.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs browserPath() lines 146-150 and receipt.config.chrome (line 322); .github/workflows/test.yml (runs `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` then tests on ubuntu-latest); README.md 'Install'
findings.failure_mode: The collector silently prefers /usr/bin/google-chrome*, /usr/bin/chromium, /usr/bin/chromium-browser over the Playwright-bundled Chromium that `npm run setup` just installed, and records `chrome: null` in the receipt when it did so (OBSERVED in my run-1 receipt and in the committed examples, which were produced with /usr/bin/google-chrome present). Consequences: (a) receipts do not say which browser/version rendered the evidence, so runs are not reproducible or comparable across machines; (b) INFERENCE: on Ubuntu, /usr/bin/chromium-browser is commonly a snap wrapper that Playwright cannot drive, so a user who ran `npm run setup` correctly still gets `browserType.launch` failures; (c) GitHub's ubuntu-latest image ships google-chrome, so CI is exercising system Chrome, not the bundled Chromium the README tells users to install — the tested path and the documented path differ. This is an assumption that holds on the owner's machine (google-chrome present) more than in general.
findings.amendment: Use the bundled Playwright Chromium by default and only use a system browser when `--chrome`/`CHROME_BIN` is given (or, at minimum, keep the auto-detect but record the resolved executable and `browser.version()` in receipt.config as `browser: { executable, version }`). Update the README sentence accordingly.
findings.mechanical_test: After capture, `python3 -c "import json;c=json.load(open('receipt.json'))['config'];assert c['browser']['version'] and c['browser']['executable']"` passes; with CHROME_BIN unset and /usr/bin/google-chrome present, the recorded executable is under the Playwright cache directory (or, if auto-detect is kept, the recorded executable is the system path — either way non-null).

findings.location: README.md 'Security defaults' bullet 'Screenshot and snapshot digests make a receipt tamper-evident' vs scripts/capture.mjs check() lines 245-260 (pngShots() filters to kind viewport/full only; accessibility_snapshot entries are never re-hashed)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: after all 8 attestations passed, I appended a line to mobile--overview.aria.yml and `check` still exited 0. The README claims snapshot digests contribute to tamper-evidence; `check` never verifies them, so a doctored accessibility snapshot (which the SKILL tells the agent to read as evidence) is accepted silently.
findings.amendment: In check(), also hash every `accessibility_snapshot` entry and emit `STALE SNAPSHOT: <path> (bytes changed since capture)` with exit code 3 when it differs or is missing; or, if snapshots are meant to be advisory, change the README sentence to 'Screenshot digests ... snapshots carry a digest for reference but are not verified by check'.
findings.mechanical_test: Add to tests/test_capture.sh after test 10b: `printf '\n#x\n' >> "$test_root/digest/test--page.aria.yml"; run 3 check "$test_root/digest/receipt.json"; grep -q 'STALE SNAPSHOT' "$test_root/stderr"`; `npm test` passes.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs attest() line 214 (note >= 10 chars) vs check() line 245 (accepts any non-empty note)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: I wrote inspections directly into a fresh receipt with note 'x' and by 'forger' and `check` printed 'OK: every screenshot inspected' and exited 0. Forgery is acknowledged in the README, but check's validity rule is looser than attest's, so a hand-written receipt passes a bar the CLI itself refuses — the two code paths disagree on what a valid attestation is.
findings.amendment: Factor the note rule into one function (`validNote = (n) => typeof n === 'string' && n.trim().length >= 10`) used by both attest() and the `invalid` filter in check(), so check reports `INVALID ATTESTATIONS` (exit 4) for sub-10-character notes.
findings.mechanical_test: Append to tests: forge a receipt copy with one inspection note 'x' and `run 4 check` on it; grep 'INVALID ATTESTATIONS' in stderr; `npm test` passes.

findings.location: SKILL.md 'Visual mode' sentence 'Attestations are append-only; a changed opinion is a new record, not an edit' vs scripts/capture.mjs check() line 265 (any record with verdict fail and matching run_id fails the gate)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: attest fail then attest pass on the same PNG → check exit 4 with FAILED ATTESTATIONS. The behaviour is correctly fail-closed, but the SKILL wording implies a later record supersedes an earlier one. An agent following the text will append a `pass` after a mistaken `fail`, get exit 4, and either be confused or start editing the JSON by hand (which the doc says never to do).
findings.amendment: Change the sentence to: 'Attestations are append-only and a `fail` is final for that run: to clear it, fix the page and re-run capture into a new run_id; append a `caveat` if you only want to add context.'
findings.mechanical_test: grep -n 'fail.*is final\|final for that run' SKILL.md returns a match; existing test 10 (fail after pass → exit 4) still passes under `npm test`.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs lines 293-304 (out-dir cleanup deletes `receipt.json` and any `*--*--{viewport,full}.png` / `*--*.aria.yml` in an existing directory); README.md and --help do not mention the deletion

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs attest() lines 221-235 (read-modify-write of receipt.json with no lock or rename)
findings.failure_mode: INFERENCE (not executed): two concurrent `attest` invocations on the same receipt (e.g. an agent parallelising eight attestations) each read the file, push one record, and write; the second write discards the first record, so a screenshot attested in good faith shows as UNINSPECTED. Append-only in name, lost-update in practice under concurrency. The SKILL does not say to attest serially.

owner_questions: Git history was NOT in the packet; your own history grep for secrets and lab strings is unverified by me. Given the CHANGELOG mentions a pre-release audit and a master→main rename, do you want an independent `git log -p | grep` for emails/hostnames/*.ts.net//home/ run on the actual repo before the flip, or are you comfortable flipping on your own grep?

Is the design intent that a `fail` attestation can never be superseded within a run (current behaviour, arguably the right fail-closed choice), or should a later record from the same `--by` be allowed to supersede? Your choice changes the SKILL wording, not just the code.

Do you want `check` to be usable on receipts moved to another machine (reviewer hand-off, CI artifact upload)? If yes, the relative-path amendment is required rather than optional; if receipts are strictly local, documenting the limitation is enough.

The committed example attestations are signed `claude-fable-5-1` and the README says the same model wrote and inspected the demo. Are you comfortable that a public reader's first concrete attestation example is the pattern the skill says not to use, or would you rather have a second model family append its own attestations to run-2 before the flip (also fixing the line-count note)?

package.json is `"private": true` and there is no npm publish path; the README install is clone + copy. Is that intentional for v0.1.0, or do you want an npx/npm story before public release (affects whether `private` should be dropped)?

Do you want a SECURITY.md / contact for reporting redaction bypasses? The README explicitly says redaction is best-effort; a public repo with that caveat and no reporting channel invites drive-by issues instead of private reports.
